title: New Here
description: New to Hope Church Winchester? Here's what to expect on your first visit, what a Sunday looks like and how to plan your visit. You'd be very welcome.
content: New here? Welcome toHope Church. We're a community from all walks of life, who genuinely care for one another and for this city. Whether you've been a Christian for decades, you're just starting to ask questions, or you're simply curious — there is a place for you here. Plan your first visit → Good to know Your first visit What to expect Coming for the first time can feel like a big step. Here's what a Sunday morning is really like — so you can walk in knowing what to expect. Come as you are There's no dress code and nothing to prepare. Wear what's comfortable — jeans and jumpers are just as welcome as anything else. About 90 minutes Our morning service runs around an hour and a half — a mix of sung worship, prayer, and a talk from the Bible, with coffee afterwards. Easy to find & park We meet at the Middle Brook Centre, just off the High Street. There's paid parking in the Middlebrook and Friarsgate car parks a moment's walk away. Coffee from 9:30am Doors open half an hour early for tea, coffee and a chance to say hello before things begin. You never have to sit alone. Kids are welcome There are age-appropriate groups for children during the service. Let a welcomer know you have little ones and they'll point you the right way. You won't be singled out You're free to simply come, watch and listen. No one will ask you to stand up, give money, or do anything you're not comfortable with. Before you come Good to know A few practical things to help you feel at home before your first visit. Sundays at Hope Sundays at Hope We gather every Sunday morning at 10am to worship, pray and open God's Word together, then again in the evening at 7:30pm to go deeper. Whichever you come to, you'll find a warm welcome and a place to belong. Learn more about Sundays → Learn about Hope Read our Welcome Booklet Find out who we are as a church, who to look out for, and everything that goes on during Sundays and throughout the week that you can get involved in. Download the booklet → Get involved Find your place here Here are a few easy, low-pressure ways to get to know us and meet people. Next: 30 Sept Newcomers Meal Enjoy a meal and meet others, including our leaders. Tim, who leads Hope Church, and some of the team share who we are — and you can ask us anything. Join the next meal → October Lunches in Homes Smaller, relaxed gatherings that bring a few newcomers together with church members over lunch — a warm, easy way to get to know people. Sign up → Every week What's on? There's a place for everyone at Hope. Discover all the ways you can find community, friendship, and purpose throughout the week. See what's on → “We had a very warm welcome at Hope Church. As it is a big church, a lot of effort goes into integrating newcomers — there are so many groups you can join, events to go to and opportunities to serve, which help you meet new people and feel part of the church family very quickly. We were also invited to welcome lunches in homes, where we met other newcomers and established church members. Everyone has been so friendly and welcoming.” Hilary & John · New to Hope Church Who we are Learn more about us Want to know our story, what we believe, and the heart behind everything we do? title: Sundays
description: What Sundays look like at Hope Church Winchester — worship at 10am at the Middle Brook Centre, kids and youth, and how to find us. Come as you are.
content: Hope Church Winchester Sundaysat Hope. Whatever brings you here, there's a warm welcome, a cup of tea, and a seat with your name on it. Here's everything you need for your first visit. 10amDoors open 9:30 Middle Brook CentreWinchester Kids groups 0–18Throughout the service 40+ languagesLive translation Get directions Sunday morning What happens on a Sunday 1 9:30am — Doors openTea, coffee, and a warm welcome from our team. Come as you are — there's no dress code and no need to know anyone. 2 10:00am — Service beginsSung worship, prayer, a Bible talk you can follow whatever your background, and time to connect. Children head to their groups after worship. 3 ~11:30am — Service endsStay for coffee and conversation and meet our team at the Connect Point. There's no rush, and someone will always be glad to answer your questions. Plan my visit → Children & young people Your kids are welcome We run groups from ages 0–18 throughout the Sunday morning service. Speak to our welcome team when you arrive and they'll help you get your children signed in and settled. Learn more about kids & youth → Age 0–4Little OnesA safe, cosy space to play with a parent or carer close by. Reception–Yr 3Lower PrimaryBible stories, games, and craft that bring faith to life. Yr 4–6Upper KidsDigging deeper together with big questions and real friendship. Yr 7–13YouthSpace to belong, have fun, and explore faith honestly. Thursdays · 7:15–9pm · Yr 7–13YouthGames, table tennis, food, and short talks on life's big questions. Sunday evenings Go deeper together On Sunday evenings we gather to slow down and grow as disciples of Jesus — making space to pray, worship, open God's Word, and go deeper in faith and friendship. All are welcome. 7:30pm Prayer & worship Teaching Community Find out what's on this Sunday → Sundays in your language We speak your language Live translation is available in over 40 languages during Sunday morning services. Scan the QR code on arrival, or ask our welcome team and we'll get you set up. Scan on arrivalConnect to live translation on your phone in seconds. Missed a Sunday?Catch up online Learn about our teaching → Sing to the Lord · PsalmsWatch → The Ancient Path · ProverbsWatch → Light in the Darkness · JudgesWatch → Getting hereFind us in Winchester Address Middle Brook CentreMiddle Brook StreetWinchester, SO23 8DQ Get directions → Parking The Middle Brook Street car park is directly opposite. Free street parking is available on many surrounding roads on Sundays. Find parking → Public transport Winchester station is a 10-minute walk. Multiple buses stop on the High Street, one minute away. Plan your journey → Accessibility & access →Step-free entry — fully wheelchair accessible throughout. →Accessible toilet on the ground floor. →Hearing loop in the main room. →A quiet, low-sensory space if you need a break. →Children welcome in the service; staffed kids' groups available. →Live English captioning & translation via our service app. First time? Your questions, answered What should I wear? Come as you are. You'll see everything from jeans and jumpers to smart-casual — there's no dress code, and no one will be looking. How long is the service? Around 90 minutes, starting at 10am. Stay for tea and coffee afterwards for as long as you like — there's no rush. What about my children? Kids are very welcome. Age-appropriate groups run during the service, led by our DBS-checked team, so children are cared for while you worship. You're also welcome to keep little ones with you. Will I have to do anything? Not at all. You're free to simply sit, watch, and take it all in. There's no pressure to sing, give, or join in with anything you're not ready for. Is the building accessible? Yes — the Middle Brook Centre is fully wheelchair accessible with step-free entry, accessible toilets, and a hearing loop. Let us know if there's anything we can do to help you feel at home. Come and say hello You'll see a friendly face The Welcome Team are by the door to help you get your bearings and show you where the kids go. After the service, find our Connect Point — a relaxed space to ask questions, find out what's on, and meet the people below. Welcome & Connect Rob, Nel and the Welcome Team are here to answer your questions and help you find ways to get involved. Kids Kirsty leads families and children's ministry, supporting parents and kids through Sunday groups and pastoral care. Community John and Lou lead community life, connecting people through groups and shared activities across the week. Youth Kate and Jim lead the youth team (ages 11–18), creating safe spaces for young people to explore faith and friendships. I'm new here → Get in touch Meet the full team → ✕

title: About
description: Who we are, what we believe and our leadership team at Hope Church Winchester — a community from every background gathering to worship and follow Jesus.
headings: Rooted in the historic Christian faith
content: About us We are Hope ChurchWinchester. A community, from a variety of backgrounds and places, who gather to worship and follow Jesus. There's space for everyone here — and we'd love you to join us as we continue to be transformed by God's love. Who we are Ordinary people, extraordinary God We're a community of Jesus followers in the heart of Winchester, gathering people from every stage of life to worship the living God. At our core, we're ordinary people transformed by an extraordinary God — and guided by the Holy Spirit, we're passionate about living out the message of the Bible together. We help people get to know and follow Jesus and grow in God's Word. We equip believers to serve Winchester, the wider UK, and support God's global mission — bringing hope, joy and blessing wherever we go. Everyone is welcome at Hope. We come as we are, and in God's kindness, he shapes us into who we're made to be. What we believe Rooted in the historic Christian faith We are an evangelical, charismatic and protestant church, holding to the historic, core and common tenets of the Christian faith as expressed in the Apostles', Nicene and Chalcedonian Creeds. We affirm the statement of faith of the Evangelical Alliance and believe the Bible to be the inspired and inerrant Word of God, sufficient in all matters of faith and practice. We believe the Holy Spirit is still operative today, and are generally reformed in our theology — with an emphasis on God's grace and justification by faith alone. We are part of Commission, a family of churches that partner in global mission, and also part of Newfrontiers. Elders Those who shepherd the church In the Bible, local churches are served by elders (see Titus 1:5–9 & 1 Timothy 3:1–7), and we have the same set-up here at Hope. Below are our current elders, alongside their wives. title: Teaching & Sermons
description: Sermons, teaching series, podcasts and worship music from Hope Church Winchester. Catch up on any series, any time — watch or listen wherever you are.
headings: Love the songs we sing on Sunday?
content: Teaching Rooted in theWord of God. Every Sunday we open the Bible together and ask what it means for our lives. Catch up on any series, any time — watch or listen wherever you are. We're a church that believes the Word of God changes lives — so we teach it deeply, clearly and joyfully. Every week, we preach from the Bible. Typically our sermon series go through a book of the Bible verse by verse — as we long to hear God speak to us today from his Word. On now Our current series Current series · Psalms Sing to the Lord This series takes a selection of the songs from Book I of Psalms. The hope is that by reflecting on what Ancient Israel corporately praised God for, that we too would be drawn up into greater adulation, adoration, and worship of God. title: Partners
description: The churches, networks and local and global mission partners we work alongside at Hope Church Winchester — loving our city and the world, practically.
headings: The wider family we belong to
content: Partners We don't dothis alone. From our church family across the world to local charities serving Winchester, we partner with organisations who share our heart for the gospel and for our city. Here's who we work alongside, and why. Church family & networks The wider family we belong to Hope Church doesn't exist in isolation. We're part of a global family of churches, networks and events that shape and support us. Newfrontiers The global family of churches we belong to, planting churches and training leaders across the world. Visit site Commission Our international family of churches within Newfrontiers, working together on planting, leadership and mission. Visit site Newday The Newfrontiers summer festival for young people, shaping the next generation of Christians. Visit site Evangelical Alliance The oldest and largest body uniting evangelical Christians and churches across the UK. Visit site Part of our church family Terry and Wendy Virgo Terry founded Newfrontiers, the global family of churches we belong to, which has grown to thousands of churches across over 70 nations. Wendy is an author and speaker who has spent decades teaching and encouraging women in churches around the world. We're blessed to have them both as part of our church family at Hope Church. Serving Winchester Loving our city, practically We support local charities doing the hands-on work of caring for people in crisis across our city and district. CAP Christians Against Poverty — free, local debt counselling and money coaching, delivered through churches. Visit site Winchester Beacon A 365-day lifeline for people experiencing homelessness across Hampshire, offering shelter and a route back to independence. Visit site Winchester Basics Bank Providing emergency food and essentials to individuals and families in crisis across the district. Visit site Street Pastors Church volunteers walking Winchester's streets at night, offering care, help and a listening ear. Visit site Winchester Pregnancy Crisis Centre WPCC offers free, impartial counselling and support to those facing an unplanned pregnancy, miscarriage, stillbirth or abortion. Visit site Acts 435 Connecting specific, practical needs with people who can meet them, one gift at a time. Visit site Emmaus Supporting people out of homelessness through meaningful work, community and a home. Visit site Miracle Street Sharing the good news of Jesus in creative, everyday ways across England and mainland Europe. Jubilee+ Equipping churches across the UK to tackle poverty and injustice, and transform their local communities. Visit site Global mission Reaching beyond our city We give towards organisations tackling poverty and sharing the gospel around the world. World Vision Child sponsorship and community development tackling the root causes of poverty worldwide. Visit site Compassion Releasing children from poverty in Jesus' name through long-term, local church partnerships. Visit site Training & safeguarding Equipping leaders, protecting people Organisations who help us train leaders well and keep our church a safe place for everyone. UCCF Universities and Colleges Christian Fellowship — supporting Christian students to live and share their faith on campus. Visit site Union School of Theology Training leaders for the church through rigorous, local-church-based theological education. Visit site thirtyone:eight The UK's leading independent Christian safeguarding charity, equipping us to protect vulnerable people. Visit site Local & independent Friends in the community Local, independent businesses who support what we do. Holy Fool Coffee A specialty coffee company training prison leavers and people overcoming social difficulty — profits fund the training. Visit site The Cornish Bakery A local food partner supporting Hope Street Cafe, our outreach ministry, supplying us with food for those living on the margins. Visit site Hope in Action The people behind the partnerships Our blog goes behind the logos — the stories of why we support these organisations and the people making a real difference across our city and beyond. Read the blog Featured story The Gospel on Wheels Hear how Miracle Street's converted double-decker bus is bringing the message of Jesus to vulnerable communities across Winchester and Southampton, partnering with local churches, councils and health services to reach the margins of society. By Steve Lee Street Pastors Six years on the streets A night out with the team caring for people on Winchester's streets. By Nigel Prior WPCC Support Without Judgment Meet the volunteers offering free, confidential support to anyone facing an unplanned pregnancy. By Emma Drake ✕
